rules.label: FPL 0-100%: Free care (100% discount)
rules.quote: Patients whose family income is at or below 100% of the FPL are eligible to receive free care.

rules.label: FPL 101-125%: Up to 80% discount
rules.quote: Patients whose family income is over 100% and below 125% of the FPL would be eligible for up to an 80% discount.

rules.label: FPL 126-150%: Up to 60% discount
rules.quote: Patients whose family income is over 125% and below 150% of the FPL would be eligible for up to a 60% discount.

rules.label: FPL 151-200%: Up to 40% discount
rules.quote: Patients whose family income is over 150% and below 200% of the FPL would be eligible for up to a 40% discount.

rules.label: FPL 201-250%: Up to 20% discount
rules.quote: Patients who family income is over 200% and below 250% of the FPL would be eligible for up to a 20% discount.

rules.label: FPL above 250%: Case-by-case for catastrophic illness or medical indigence
rules.quote: Patients whose family income exceeds 250% of the FPL will generally not be deemed eligible for financial assistance; but, may be considered for financial assistance on a case-by-case basis based on their specific circumstances, such as catastrophic illness or medical indigence, at the discretion of RGH.

application.quote: A patient has 240 days after the date of first billing to submit data for financial assistance.

eca_not_before.quote: No extraordinary collection action will be taken before 182 days from the first bill.

notes: Policy applies to hospital, clinics, and employed providers (inpatient, ER, family practice, orthopedics by Dr. Hunter, surgery by Thompson, anesthesia by Monarch). Excludes non-employee providers: Colorado Imaging Associates radiologists, San Luis Valley Health specialists, Health One cardiology, Vascular Institute of the Rockies, surgeries by Chang and Marshall-Rodriguez.
Discounted rates shall not exceed amounts generally billed to commercially insured patients (look-back method using Medicare fee-for-service and private insurer claims).
Financial need re-evaluated every 12 months or if financial situation changes.
Application requires documentation: tax return, W-2, pay stubs (6 months), bank statements (3 months), employer letter, SSA award letter, or proof of direct deposit.
Accounts eligible for financial assistance addressed within 240 days of first bill; accounts may be considered up to 6 months prior to determination and up to 1 year after.
RGH notifies patient in writing within 30 days of completed application.
Collection activity suspended during financial assistance review; resumes if partial adjustment, non-cooperation, or ineligibility.
ECA not initiated for emergency care (emergency, inpatient, ancillary services). If account in ECA later qualifies, RGH reverses ECA.
Patients who owe balance after insurance or are higher income and do not qualify may be pursued for litigation in Colorado.
Policy complies with Colorado DSH and Colorado Hospital Discount Care rules.
Application available in English and Spanish.
Self-pay accounts outsourced; reviewed for further action if not paid or satisfactory arrangements not made.

findings.title: Covers everyone Colorado's Hospital Discounted Care protects

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: Patients and their households are eligible for Hospital Discounted Care if, during the required screening and application processes, they are determined to: Have a total household income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG), and Be residents of the State of Colorado.
IF REQUESTED BY THE PATIENT, A HEALTH-CARE FACILITY SHALL SCREEN AN INSURED PATIENT FOR DISCOUNTED CARE

findings.summary: Inconclusive: 1 of the model's rules were dropped by the quote and meaning checks, so a missing rule may be our error. Z3's case: A household of 3 earning $34,400 a year (125.9% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, uninsured, owing $10,000 meets every requirement, but no rule of this policy grants them help. Colorado law makes them eligible for Hospital Discounted Care.

findings.title: Ignores assets for Colorado-protected households

law.quote: THE METHODOLOGY MUST NOT CONSIDER A PATIENT'S ASSETS.

findings.summary: Proved: for households Colorado's law protects, savings and assets never changes the outcome.
findings.domain: every household of 1–12 people, income $0–$1M, assets $0–$10M, and every combination of the yes/no facts (pairs of households)

findings.title: Doesn't require a Medicaid application first

law.quote: DENY DISCOUNTED CARE ON THE BASIS THAT THE PATIENT HAS NOT APPLIED FOR ANY PUBLIC BENEFITS PROGRAM

findings.summary: Proved: for households Colorado's law protects, whether they applied for Medicaid or other public programs never changes the outcome.
findings.domain: every household of 1–12 people, income $0–$1M, assets $0–$10M, and every combination of the yes/no facts (pairs of households)

findings.title: No collection lawsuits or garnishment before day 182

law.quote: NO MEDICAL CREDITOR COLLECTING ON A DEBT FOR HOSPITAL SERVICES SHALL ENGAGE IN ANY PERMISSIBLE EXTRAORDINARY COLLECTION ACTIONS UNTIL ONE HUNDRED EIGHTY-TWO DAYS AFTER THE DATE THE PATIENT RECEIVES HOSPITAL SERVICES.

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: begin sending bills beginning 46 days after the patient's date of service or date of discharge

findings.summary: Proved: whatever day the first bill goes out, the policy's own timeline never allows a collection action before day 182 after care.
findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 46 to day 400

findings.title: Accepts applications for at least 181 days after care

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: Patients may complete a screening at any time within at least 181 days after their date of service or discharge, whichever is later

findings.summary: Proved: the application window never closes before day 181 after care.
findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 0 to day 400

findings.title: Insured patients get 45 days after their first post-insurance bill

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: At least 45 days from the date of the first bill after the patient's insurance adjustment, even if that date falls outside the normal 181-day window.

findings.summary: Proved: the window always stays open at least 45 days past the first bill.
findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 0 to day 400

findings.title: Payment plans capped at 4% of monthly income, done after 36 payments

law.quote: THE PATIENT IS NOT PAYING MORE THAN FOUR PERCENT OF THE PATIENT'S MONTHLY HOUSEHOLD INCOME ON A BILL FROM A HEALTH-CARE FACILITY
AFTER A CUMULATIVE THIRTY-SIX MONTHS OF PAYMENTS, CONSIDER THE PATIENT'S BILL PAID IN FULL

findings.summary: The policy states no payment-plan terms to check. Colorado's 4% / 36-month limits apply anyway.

findings.title: Application window of 240 days after the first bill (501(r))

law.quote: ends on the later of the 240th day after the date that the first post-discharge billing statement for the care is provided

findings.summary: Skipped: 501(r) applies to tax-exempt hospitals, and we haven't verified this hospital's status (many rural Colorado hospitals are public districts).

findings.title: No collection actions in the first 120 days after the first bill (501(r))

law.quote: for at least 120 days from the date the hospital facility provides the first post-discharge billing statement for the care

findings.summary: Skipped: 501(r) applies to tax-exempt hospitals, and we haven't verified this hospital's status (many rural Colorado hospitals are public districts).

findings.title: Earning less never means getting less help
findings.summary: Inconclusive: 1 of the model's rules were dropped by the quote and meaning checks, so a missing rule may be our error. Z3's case: A household of 3 earning $41,153 a year (150.6% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, uninsured, owing $10,000 gets no help; the same household earning more, at 151.00% of the poverty line, gets 40% off. The written income bands leave a gap between them.
